answerNotes.TEA: Tea is made by steeping leaves in water. Herbal drinks are often called teas too, although the plants can be different.
answerNotes.ICE: Ice is solid water. It absorbs heat as it melts, which helps cool a drink.
answerNotes.LEMON: Lemon juice is sour. Zest is the thin colored outer peel used for flavor, not the thick white layer beneath it.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.CHILL: Chill means lower a food's temperature. It does not necessarily mean freeze it solid.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.

answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
